text: {"kind":"final","content":"{\"answer\":\"Root Route’s data: today 70.99917252792718% on-time, 48,340 deliveries, 14,019 late, penalties of $872,460, handling costs of $476,646, 9 at-risk accounts and at-risk revenue $14,200,000. Carrier problems affect 10,030 deliveries (bad carrier lanes 7,895) and the bad-lane late rate is 45.9%. Route overruns affect 2,880 deliveries and their late rate is 62.6%. Fixing carrier lanes + routes would replay to 80.4% on-time, avoiding 4,523 late deliveries and $409,897 cost. The routing contract (carrier lanes) is the portion of that: carrier lanes only replay is 77.4% on-time, avoiding 3,091 late and $282,161 cost. Other causes before pickup are large: incomplete addresses 5,994 orders (late rate 64.6%), cut-off misses 4,826 (late rate 61.0%), and non‑nearest/stock issues together affect thousands of shipments. Fixing addresses + cut-off + stock would replay to 87.8% on-time, avoiding 8,112 late and $801,412 cost. Suggestion (from the data, not a decision): the evidence shows fixing pre-pickup causes (Address + cut-off + stock → 87.8% on-time) gives a higher on-time rate than fixing carrier lanes + routes (Carrier lanes + routes → 80.4% on-time). That comparison is the key data point; changing the balance would require materially higher avoided late deliveries or costs from lanes/routes in the replay. The decision stays with Halcyon.\",\"refused\":false}"}
